action: Identify and reassess the owner's green-object screenshot.
observation: The image exactly matches the corrosive volatile-bottle diagnostic. The two-mesh procedural object has no surface textures; the prior smoothing made its entire class-colored shell glossy and green rather than solving its lack of detail. The owner rejected the appearance.
decision: Reopen the bottle and its hazard variants; use a detailed, mostly neutral industrial shell with limited class color as a candidate, subject to real-renderer review.
next: Compare the generated material on the production geometry at useful close and chase views, then inspect every hazard color and pickup/payload route.
evidenceScope: Owner-provided image matched to a synthetic real-producer diagnostic, source inspection, and an unreviewed generated image; not a natural encounter.
performance: Existing diagnostic submits two meshes; the proposed texture's actual GPU cost and frame-time effect are unmeasured.

action: Compare the generated pressure-vessel surface and Astra geometry on payload and pickup diagnostics, including three hazard colors.
observation: The textured shell and smoother, seated cage look more manufactured than the rejected neon sphere while keeping two observed target submissions. The hazard colors are much too faint at the chase camera, so explosive, corrosive and superdense versions are difficult to distinguish at useful range.
decision: Do not promote this candidate. Test a small class-colored physical marking and localized low-intensity emission while keeping the shell detailed and preserving the existing warning semantics.
next: Inspect the warning treatments in the same renderer at close and chase scales and retain only a readable, restrained result.
evidenceScope: One synthetic renderer session using real factory construction and temporary texture/geometry variants; pickup rows exercise the factory branch by changing the diagnostic entity type. Not a natural encounter.
performance: Two observed target draw submissions per view; memory, loading, shader cost and gameplay frame time remain unmeasured.

action: Replace the monochrome shell with one generated steel surface and preserve class cues on a seated containment band.
observation: The production visual factory loads the 512px texture and renders all four stamped classes in the preview; cryogenic previously fell back to amber and now uses the existing cyan cue. The surface reads as fabricated metal at close range and colored bands remain distinguishable in the recorded chase views.
decision: Integrate as an improvement, but keep full visual review, natural gameplay and performance acceptance open.
next: Check the normal New Game route and an actual cargo encounter, and continue the requested multi-angle asset review.
evidenceScope: Current production factory and texture loader with synthetic producer entities in the game renderer. Pickup construction is exercised; no natural jettison is claimed.
performance: Two observed target submissions and 1020 triangles versus 1036 in the previous geometry; one shared 512px image adds texture memory and can upload late. Frame time is unmeasured.

action: Compare the actual delayed-texture fallback with a neutral shell and 32px and 64px copies of the generated pressure-vessel surface.
observation: The live fallback reproduces the rejected bright monochrome sphere. A neutral shell leaves the class-colored containment band visible, but remains untextured. Both reduced image copies lose close-up hatch detail and look blurry; at the recorded small view they offer no meaningful improvement over the full surface.
decision: Reject the embedded low-resolution copies. Use a neutral shared placeholder while the detailed surface loads and investigate bounded recovery after a transient failure; do not treat the fallback as final-quality art.
next: Integrate the shared placeholder and retry, check all four hazard bands and the texture upgrade, then review the natural cargo route and remaining asset variants.
evidenceScope: Controlled synthetic real-producer entities in the game renderer, with the image request held; no natural encounter or frame-time measurement.
performance: All compared views submitted two target draws. The 32px and 64px copies would add approximately 5.3 KiB and 21.3 KiB of mipmapped RGBA GPU memory respectively; gameplay performance is unmeasured.
